# Late tear-out release leaves the pane in the provisional vessel chrome

## Context

Found by @neo-opus-grace while verifying #19990 (headless Chrome through the Neural Link fixture), defect-note 2026-10-22 15:10Z; identical on `dev` 8abdcf978c, so it predates the #19990 work. Filed by me at Grace's request, as part of the Workstation patch-release board ([milestone v13.3.1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/milestone/12)). Grace takes the implementation after #20006 merges, so `VesselWorkspace.mjs` keeps one writer.

**Observed** (Grace, dev 8abdcf978c): press Audit in the flagship Workstation, drag past the viewport so a vessel opens, wait for the vessel's `domcontentloaded` plus ~1.5 s, then release.
- `lastCrossWindowTransfer` reads `{applied: true, errors: ["Popup Workspace workstation-vessel:audit left its pane in provisional chrome"]}`.
- The App worker logs `PopupWorkspace: the landed pane's repaint render failed` with `Symbol(Neo.isDestroyed)`.
- The existing tear-out specs release on a different timing and stay green.

Not re-run by the filer yet (the seat is running the full suite for the release gate); the reproduction is Grace's, with her steps above. Observation and inference are kept apart below.

## The Problem

A tear-out has two stage targets in time: the provisional chrome a born vessel shows at once (#19210), and the committed projection's host that replaces it. The commit path (`mountVesselWorkspace`, moving arm) assumes the committed projection's refresh moves the staged pane out of the chrome by identity, then retires the empty chrome. When the release comes late, the retirement finds the pane still inside the chrome and the mount throws `left its pane in provisional chrome`; the catch releases the pane detached (`releasePanes: true`), the error propagates to the transfer's caller, which records `applied: true` with the error and skips the commit's later steps. The second log line (`repaint render failed`, `isDestroyed`) is consistent with the released pane being destroyed or re-created underneath `repaintLandedPane`: inferred, not measured.

Why late matters (inference, for the fix to confirm): with an early release the vessel's Workspace host is still projecting when the pane is staged, so the reconciler's same-window DOM move carries the pane into the host; after ~1.5 s the host has settled, the staged pane arrives after the projection the mount awaits, and nothing moves it. The failure is an ordering between two asynchronous arrivals, not a size or key problem.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`
  - `registerVesselWorkspaceTarget` (:527) → `mountVesselWorkspace(state.workspaceId)` (:539).
  - `mountVesselWorkspace` (:753): `moving = chrome?.parent === target && Boolean(body?.items.length)` (:759); the moving arm awaits `host.refreshPromise`, then requires `retireProvisionalVesselChrome(state.windowId)` to return true (:779–781); the catch retires with `{releasePanes: true}` and rethrows (:786–787).
  - `retireProvisionalVesselChrome` (:847) returns `false` while the chrome's card body holds a pane unless `releasePanes` (:854–858).
  - The transfer callers record the receipt: `lastCrossWindowTransfer = {applied: committed, errors: [...]}` (:1456) and `{applied: false, errors: [error.message]}` (:1496).
- `apps/workstation/view/PopupWorkspace.mjs` `repaintLandedPane` (:211–227) logs the repaint failure of a surviving pane.
- Precedent: #19264 fixed the committed tear-out re-rendering the pane instead of moving its node out of the chrome; #19186 fixed a parked vessel outliving the commit that consumed its pane. This ticket is the remaining timing arm of the same seam.

Design authority: ADR 0029 §2.8.2 (the gesture outcome machine: a committed target completes its commit or rolls back; a receipt that says `applied: true` while carrying a commit error and skipped steps is neither) and §2.8.3 (vessel lifecycle and admission).

## The Fix

The owner's call (Grace, after #20006); the direction that fits the seam:
- Make the moving arm of `mountVesselWorkspace` independent of arrival order: when the committed projection's refresh has already run, move the staged pane out of the chrome by identity into the host's dock tab container (the #19264 move, not a re-render), then retire the chrome; or await the pane's arrival in the host before retiring.
- A commit that cannot place the pane must not leave `applied: true` with errors: either it completes, or the receipt says `applied: false` and the pane returns to its source (§2.8.2).
- #20006 rewrites `registerVesselWorkspaceTarget` (adds `workspaceKey`, keys the vessel by its minted Group key), so the error text and the entry point change; this fix lands after it, in the same function family.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: In a Workstation NL e2e (a new arm in a tear-out spec under `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/`), a main-sourced tear-out released after the vessel's `domcontentloaded` plus 1.5 s commits: `lastCrossWindowTransfer.applied === true` with `errors` empty, the pane is mounted inside the vessel's dock tab container, and the provisional chrome is gone. Red on base, green at head.
- [ ] AC-2: The same run logs no `left its pane in provisional chrome` and no `repaint render failed` error in any window's console; the arm asserts on the console itself, since the `workerErrors` fixture does not see main-thread errors from other windows.
- [ ] AC-3: The existing early-release tear-out arms stay green at head.
- [ ] AC-4: A unit arm on `mountVesselWorkspace` covers the late ordering: the chrome still holds the pane after the host's refresh, and the mount either moves it or reports `applied: false` with no orphaned pane.

## Out of Scope

- #20006 (the vessel's key and registry identity).
- #20017 (the warm-reload remount race).
- The repaint layer itself (`repaintLandedPane`) beyond the log it emits here.

## Avoided Traps

- Retiring with `releasePanes: true` in the moving arm unconditionally: it detaches a live pane and re-renders it, the #19264 defect in reverse.
- Swallowing the thrown error so the receipt reads clean: the pane would still sit in the wrong parent.
- A fixed wait before the commit: the race is between two arrivals, and a wait moves the window instead of closing it.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-23T00:09:53Z

**Reproduced on current `dev` `9cad83b350` (after #20019), 3/3, with the original steps.** Audit dragged past the viewport, release at vessel `domcontentloaded` + 1.5 s:

- Receipt: `{"applied":true,"errors":["Popup Workspace workstation-vessel:audit left its pane in provisional chrome"]}`, as filed.
- The `repaint render failed` log no longer appears (gone since #20019's repaint-settlement change).
- **End state is correct:** the Audit pane is in the vessel's DOM, visible, inside `.workstation-vessel-dock-host` and its `.neo-dashboard-dock-tabs`. The window shows one header ("Audit") and no provisional chrome.

Mechanism, read from the code:
1. On a late release the vessel connects before the terminal. `afterTearOutWindowConnect` finds no owner, so it stages the pane into the provisional chrome.
2. At the terminal, `onTearOutDocumentChange` transfers the item, adopts the pane, then calls `registerVesselWorkspaceTarget` → `mountVesselWorkspace` (moving arm).
3. That arm awaits `host.refreshPromise`. The transfer's projection has not taken the staged pane out of the chrome, so `retireProvisionalVesselChrome` returns false and the arm throws.
4. Its catch retires the chrome with `releasePanes: true`. The host's projection then renders the released pane. That is a re-render, not the #19264 DOM move, so the pane's DOM-held state (scroll positions and the like) does not survive. The receipt keeps the error although the commit landed.

Still open, and the fix's first step: why the transfer's projection leaves a staged pane in the chrome. An early release never stages, which is why the existing arms stay green.

Impact for the v13.3.1 record: no lost or misplaced pane. A late release gets a spurious receipt error, plus a re-render where a move was due.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-23T07:39:59Z

**Cause named. Correction to my comment of 00:09Z: the pane is moved, not re-rendered.** The projection takes the staged pane out of the chrome correctly. The error comes from a second mount of the same vessel.

**Trace** (dev `3317a124d9`, the late-release arm with scratch tracing, ms from the commit):

| t | What happens |
|---|---|
| +0 | `onTearOutDocumentChange` commits; the pane is staged in the chrome. |
| +8 | `adoptPane` → `afterNativeOwnerChange` → `registerVesselWorkspaceTarget` → **mount #1** starts (moving arm). |
| +8 | `onTearOutDocumentChange`'s own `registerVesselWorkspaceTarget` → **mount #2** starts. Its early return requires `state.host.parent === app.mainView`, but mount #1 has not added the host yet. |
| +42 | Both mounts add the host and await its refresh. |
| +143 | The vessel's projection lands: the chrome body is empty (`mount:refreshed body: ""`). Mount #1 retires the chrome. Mount #2's `retireProvisionalVesselChrome` finds no chrome, returns `false`, and throws `left its pane in provisional chrome`. |

So the receipt error comes from a mount that lost the race to retire an already-empty chrome. A witness marks the staged DOM node before the release. The node keeps its mark after the commit on dev too, so the pane moves; my earlier "re-render" was an inference that this measurement refutes.

**Fix:** a second binding of the same vessel window joins the mount in flight instead of starting another one (`registerVesselWorkspaceTarget`). PR follows.

**Reproducer, AC-1's arm** (`WorkstationTearOutLateReleaseNL.spec.mjs`): release once the vessel has staged the pane. The condition is the late order; no fixed wait. Dev: 3 of 3 red. Fix: 5 of 5 green.
